chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukayr, from Durays, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic
And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they are associating others (with Him)
He said: It is the shirk of obedience, and it is not the shirk of worship.
And regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic
And among men is he who worships Allah on a corner (superficially)
He said: The verse was revealed regarding a man, then it applies to his followers.
Then I said: Every one who establishes anything besides you is from those who worship Allah superficially?
He said: Yes, and it can be purely that.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between shirk of obedience and shirk of worship in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between major idolatry and 'shirk of obedience,' where the majority of believers associate partners with God by following the rulings of scholars or leaders. He further elucidates the concept of worshipping 'on a corner' (al-harf) from Surah al-Hajj, noting that while it often describes a person and their followers, it can also apply to anyone who establishes a religious authority or practice distinct from the Imams, even if it remains pure monotheism.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zureys, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
regarding the Words of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic
[12:106] And most of them do not believe in Allah except they are associating others (with Him).
Heasws said: ‘This is the Shirk (association) of obedience, and it is not Shirk (association) of worship’.
And about the Words of the Mighty and Majestic
[22:11] And among men is the one who worships Allah superficially.
So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The Verse was Revealed regarding a man, then it occurred also to be regarding his followers’.

Then I said: ‘Every one who establishes anyone besides you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, so he is from the ones who worships Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> superficially?’.
So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, and it is purely that’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus from ibn Bukayr from Durays from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)
who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy,
‘Most of them do not believe in Allah; they are but pagans,’ [12:106]
the Imam said, ‘Al-Shirk (paganism) is obedience and it is not worship,’
and the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy,
‘ . . . certain people worship Allah to achieve worldly gains. . . .,’ [22:11]
the Imam said, ‘A verse comes down about a man and then it applies to his followers.’
I then said, ‘Do those who appoint others (as people possessing Divine Authority) instead of you ( Ahl al-Bayt) worship for worldly gains?’
The Imam said, ‘Yes, at certain cases it is just that ( al - Shirk ).’”
